A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Schur-complement approach to CLIP decomposition and diversity evaluation. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison; visual inspection resolves extraction problems in figure content.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–F report original generation, captioning, clustering, concept-removal, typographic-attack, and diversity-evaluation results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–E retain original empirical results and add doctor-demographic controls, cat-and-dog comparisons, and typographic-attack diversity analyses.

M1.justification: The decomposition, optimization objective, and entropy construction remain. However, Remark 1 and the paragraph preceding Equation 7 change the correction matrix from C_IT C_TT^-1 to C_TI C_TT^-1. Since v1 already uses the latter expression in Proposition 1 and its proof, the PDFs leave unclear whether this changes the intended computation or attempts to repair inconsistent subscripts.

E1.justification: v2 adds doctor age/gender populations, IdenProf doctor reference images, and cat-and-dog scenarios contrasting breed and scene diversity. These extend the existing text-to-image evaluation coverage; the animal/object, captioning, typographic ImageNet, and MSCOCO evaluations remain.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares diversity against Vendi. v2 evaluates RKE in Figures 2 and 4 and adds Recall and Coverage, including to the retained cat-breed experiment in Figure 5. The naive-subtraction baseline already existed in v1 Appendix E. Conversely, the traffic-sign clustering comparison drops its uncorrected-CLIP panel between v1 Figure 5 and v2 Figure 20.

E3.justification: v2 introduces complementary controls varying doctor demographics with fixed prompts and varying prompt specificity across separately generated sets from a fixed intended image distribution. It also adds class-count sweeps under typographic attacks and reference-based evaluation using IdenProf doctors and ImageNet cats. Existing settings such as 1,000 images per cat breed, 2,000 Fourier features, and 5,000 MSCOCO captions remain.

E4.justification: Figures 2–4 add controlled case studies probing attribution of diversity to prompts versus generators. Appendix C and Figure 21 add diversity sensitivity to class count under text overlays and before/after saliency maps. The cosine-kernel checks and naive-subtraction ablations were already present; the traffic-sign clustering demonstration is reduced.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that the four doctor-image sets in Figure 4 use different seeds. This describes the new experimental design, not repeated estimates of the same condition or an established increase in replication. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or explicit uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New results include cat-and-dog SCE-I scores of 2.7 versus 1.7 despite Vendi scores of 20.5 versus 37.1, doctor SCE-I scores spanning 2.22–4.74, and reference-metric and saliency results. The retained Gaussian cat-breed comparison changes its Vendi curve and removes its text-side SCE panels. The cassette-player frequencies of 78.69% and 12.00% already appear in v1 Figure 17, and the MSCOCO model-comparison plot is unchanged.

T1.justification: The correction-matrix expressions in Remark 1 and the introduction to Equation 7 swap C_IT for C_TI without changing the covariance definitions, a localized mathematical revision rather than equivalent notation. Proposition 1 and the appendix proofs, including the shared-eigenvector assumption in Appendix A.2, remain unchanged. The text-side SCE definition moves into Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: separating prompt-induced and model-induced diversity, evaluating intrinsic diversity with SCE, and removing specified concepts from CLIP embeddings. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving demographic bias, prompt specificity, and saliency under text overlays, and explicitly limits the diffusion examples to illustrating embeddings rather than direct image editing. It also describes retained cassette-player label frequencies as misclassification rates, although Figure 10 reports prediction frequencies rather than error rates.

D1.justification: v2 supplies prompts and reference-subset information for its new comparisons. It removes Section 5's explicit statement that CLIP correction experiments use a matrix computed on the MSCOCO training split; Appendix B still names captioned MSCOCO without specifying the split. The code-access statement and existing Fourier-feature settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for IdenProf and ImageNet and removes the SDXL paper reference, although SDXL experiments remain. Other reference changes largely reflect renumbering, and the related-work discussion and central positioning against unconditional diversity metrics remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized around a diversity example, with its former clustering explanation moved into Section 5. The experimental narrative is substantially rewritten and reordered, the captioning discussion moves from its own appendix into the main text, and the text-side entropy definition moves to Appendix A.2. The abstract and conclusion remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 moves Figure 1 onto the title page, adds diversity-control and saliency displays, and substantially rearranges clustering, diffusion, and t-SNE figures. The combined cat/animal diversity figure is split between the main text and appendix, retained classification results are redisplayed in the main text, and the traffic-sign gallery loses its baseline and fourth-cluster panels.

improvement.justification: The added demographic controls, broader metric comparisons, and saliency analysis strengthen empirical support beyond v1's existing demonstrations and clarify intended behavior. These gains are tempered by unresolved correction-matrix inconsistencies and the newly misleading description of prediction frequencies as error rates. The net improvement is useful but limited.
